To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Qa-11 leader-derived peptide Qdm is a TAP-dependent epitope, that this TAP dependence is not due to a failure of the leader to gain access to protease activity in the ER, and that a single amino acid substitution in the leader can alter its trafficking to allow for TAP-independent processing.

the Qa-11 binding epitope Qdm derived from the leader segment of a class I molecule is a poor substrate for the proteases of the endoplasmatic reticulum and that the Qdm peptide is not transported by TAP.

1) the Qdm leader epitope is not processed by ER proteases, 2) the DL does not gain access the ER, and 3) changing an Arg at P7 in the leader to a Cys allows the Qdm epitopes to enter the ER and gain TAP independence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors controlling the trafficking and processing of a leader-derived peptide.
the mechanisms that govern the trafficking, processing and presentation of a leader-derived peptide.
the factors controlling the processing and presentation of leader-derived peptides by class Ia molecules and the mechanisms involved in their trafficking into the ER.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the trafficking of leader-derived epitopes is determined by a combination of the ability of the cell to trim the peptide to its appropriate length and its ability to gain access to and translocate across the ER membrane.
TAP is required for Qdm presentation, because the leader peptide is not processed by the proteases of the ER, and that the leader peptide is unable to gain access to ER.
Qdm is presented by class Ib molecules in the ER and is dependent on TAP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the trafficking and processing of a leader-derived epitope is determined by both the proteolytic activity of the ER and the ability of a leader to gain access to it.
Qdm is not accessible to proteases resident in T2 cell ER lumen.
Qdm can be presented by class Ib molecules in the absence of TAP when the leader peptide has a Cys at position 7.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the trafficking of leader-derived peptides can be controlled by the amino acid sequence of their C terminus.
leader peptide presentation by class Ib molecules is dependent on the ability of the peptide to access the lumen of ER and that TAP is required to transport the peptide to the ER.
leader-derived peptides can be presented in a TAP-dependent or -independent manner.
